song.title: April Showers
song.author: Mark, Helen and Naomi Johnson
song.summary: A song of four simple, easy-to-perform parts, that build and overlay. It’s great fun hearing all the parts come together, and good for listening and holding individual melodies. Create the arrival and fading of a seasonal shower, and enjoy the changes of dynamic along the way.
song.teachingTips:
• This is a great song to cheer everyone up on a rainy day! Each of the four parts is easy to learn and will sound impressive sung altogether.
  • Teach all the parts to everyone first before splitting the class into four groups and allocating each a verse. You might like to have equally-sized groups or small groups for verses 1-3 and a larger group for verse 4 – it’s up to you.
  • Encourage the children to listen carefully to the track to help them know when to come in. At first it will be helpful to conduct the entries.
  • Make sure that the verse 1 singers put the ‘p’ on the end of each ‘drip, drop’ and remember to watch the conductor for their final line, ‘we’ve gotta stop’.
  • You might like to try singing without the backing track and experimenting with the groups starting and stopping at different times.
  • A performance with children wearing wellies and raincoats, and some choreography involving umbrellas, would be great fun!

assembly.title: The World Around
assembly.description: From the tallest trees, to the something you can only see with a microscope, this assembly encourages us to notice, appreciate and be thankful for the world around us.

assembly.title: Happy Endings
assembly.description: This assembly explores setbacks we might encounter in our lives and the characteristics needed to overcome them.

resources.title: Rainy-Day Percussion
resources.content:
[{"key":"9bc2f9af8a6e8a85","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"
  • To explore texture and timbre
  • To perform in four parts as an ensemble
  • To improvise a percussive accompaniment
","title":"What’s achievable","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/green-star-1614702483w2iKm.png"}},{"key":"4397891b95076e4d","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Percussion instruments, e.g. xylophones, rainmakers, shakers

","title":"What you need","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/blue-wrench-16147025258WedI.png"}},{"key":"71d44367ff908d9c","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Discuss how you could represent rain sounds using percussion instruments and body percussion. Would metallic or wooden instruments sound best? Can the children make a ‘drip’ sound with their mouths, as if they were fish? You might like to listen to the backing track on its own for inspiration.

As a class, decide which instruments/sounds (timbres) would be best for each verse. As a starting point, you could try the following:

  • Verse 1: mouths
  • Verse 2: fingers patting on desks
  • Verse 3: xylophones playing the ‘it’s raining, it’s pouring’ motif using the notes C A F
  • Verse 4: rainmakers and shakers for ‘April showers’

Try performing along with the vocal track, or splitting the class in half and having half singing, half playing.

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"71c6092693e59585","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

resources.summary: A chance to explore and improvise raindrop sound effects using percussion instruments and body percussion. This activity also provides a great opportunity for discussing texture, timbre and dynamics as the four parts gradually enter and then stop, representing the passing shower.

resources.title: April-Shower Composition
resources.content:
[{"key":"2cd18fca2fb74afd","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Play the children the backing track to April Showers<\/em> and then this video of ‘Little April Shower’ <\/em>from Disney’s Bambi<\/em>: <\/p>\n","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"928e4d10fef73b70","layout":"video","attributes":{"url":"www.youtube.com\/watch?v=S-FUcrQhTBY","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"71c01a3f85c36ff1","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

In both cases, ask the children to listen very carefully to how rain is depicted in the music. In the video, talk about how the rain starts slowly with the clarinet’s single notes, then how the tempo increases when the triangle and voices come in. Listen out for the descriptive storm section in the middle in the minor key with cymbal crashes for the lightning, and then the return to the happy major song at the end (giving it an ABA structure). Use both tracks as inspiration for your own class April-shower composition<\/strong>.<\/p>\n","title":"","noMargin":false}}]

resources.title: Rain Poetry
resources.content:
[{"key":"083609fe9278cfe6","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Read some poems about rain and see if you can pick out the imagery or other literary devices that the poet has used to create atmosphere. Write a list of the most effective phrases and see if the children can incorporate them into a piece of descriptive writing about rain. Play a YouTube video of rain sounds and images to inspire them whilst they write!

  • Spring Storm, William Carlos Williams
  • The Rain, William Henry Davies
  • Rain, Robert Louis Stevenson
  • Rainy Nights, Irene Thompson
